Subject: Request: isolation evidence workbook + diagram index for Dedicated/Private

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick response on our intake call last week. As part of AstraNova's SOC 2 + SIG intake we need a consolidated "isolation evidence workbook" that maps Redwood's Dedicated and Private deployment isolation controls to the SIG/CAIQ/SOC 2 criteria. Specifically we need:

- A short index of network diagrams (PDF) that shows: control plane partitioning, tenant egress paths, edge demarcation, and any air-gapped/on-prem variants.
- A single workbook (xlsx) that maps evidence artifacts to SIG questions and SOC 2 CCs (column for artifact name, storage/retention location, attestation owner, and a brief summary).
- Any supporting visio/diagram source files if possible (we sometimes need to annotate).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these artifacts by EOD Tue 2027-08-31 PT? If you have an internal stub or index already, please send the current version and we can flag follow-ups.

Also helpful: a brief paragraph describing how Redwood routes requests between hosted/dedicated/private and what fallback/segmentation controls protect customer workloads. This can be short (3-5 bullets).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Oliver Grant
Senior Auditor, AstraNova

Oliver,

Appreciate the clear ask — we can deliver an initial package by EOD Tuesday (end of day 2027-08-31 PT). I'm attaching the first-pass artifacts and a short narrative; Ben will own the final packaging.

Attached (first pass):
- 20270830-isolation-diagrams.pdf (includes Dedicated vs Private overlays; label legend included)
- isolation-evidence-workbook-astranova.xlsx (mapping SIG questions -> artifacts -> owner)
- network-zone-mapping.vsdx (Visio source for the diagrams)

Quick routing/segmentation bullets (for your intake):
- Smart routing: requests are routed by policy (region, capacity tier, customer tenancy) — control plane and data plane are logically separated; control plane endpoints are not on tenant-facing networks.
- Tenant fencing: Dedicated pools use network-level tenant fencing with dedicated VLANs and strict egress ACLs; Private deployments can be deployed in-customer VPCs with explicit peering and no public internet ingress.
- Caching & fallbacks: inference cache/prefix stores are per-deployment and encrypted; automatic model fallback only occurs to pre-approved, compatible variants and inherits the same egress policies.
- Audit & visibility: per-request telemetry (traces, token-level cost) and audit logs are stored in a customer-scoped logging sink for Private and encrypted audit buckets for Dedicated.

Notes:
- The workbook has many "TBD" cells where we have legacy artifacts to surface; Kimberly and Ben are cc'd to confirm owners and the retention/hosting location.
- If you need a one-page narrative tailored to SOC 2 control IDs, say which control IDs you prefer and we'll produce that as a separate sheet.

Link to working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_exAMPLE-folder (shared with your auditor domain)

Best,

Stephanie Nguyen

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: isolation evidence workbook + diagram index for Dedicated/Private

Stephanie / Ben —

Thanks for pushing this out. I reviewed the attached PDF and workbook; a few quick edits we should make before final delivery to AstraNova:

1) Diagram labels: the "control plane partitioning" callout on page 3 needs to clarify the control-plane management VPC is in a separate tenant domain (we currently label it as "control-plane" but auditors ask for isolation justification).
2) Egress attestation: the workbook references "egress ACLs" but doesn't state the default-stale retention location for egress logs (we keep a 90-day ephemeral copy in our ops cluster and a 7-year archive in encrypted long-term storage for audited customers — need to confirm wording).
3) Private deployment note: add a short sentence explaining that Private (VPC) installations can optionally route audit logs to the customer's KMS+S3/GCS and that we provide HSM integrations on request.

I've drafted suggested wording below for the control-plane paragraph — paste into the workbook under "Control Plane Description" and I'll review: 

"Control plane services (orchestration, scheduling, model catalog) run in a management VPC that is logically and network-isolated from tenant-serving planes. Control plane endpoints do not accept tenant data and are restricted to management identities; all control-plane communications are authenticated with mTLS and limited by IAM policies. For Dedicated, the management VPC is hosted in Redwood-managed accounts with strict egress ACLs; for Private, the management components are deployed into the customer's management VPC and governed by customer-side network rules."

Ben — can you confirm the egress log retention phrasing and whether we can attach an example retention-policy PDF for AstraNova? I can also add the CAIQ/SIG mapping tab if you want me to.

Kimberly Park
Product Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
